fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. The LORD says, "Come out of her, My people!" (Jeremiah 51:45). Two things stand out to me here: He calls them "My people," and the word is to leave.

I get the thought, because loyalty is a good instinct. But the verse never sends anyone to the walls. The LORD says, "Come out of her, My people!" (Jeremiah 51:45). That's like hearing the fire alarm and staying behind to guard the front desk. Nope, you head out.
Lives is the word. The LORD says, "Save your lives, each of you, from the fierce anger of the LORD." (Jeremiah 51:45). Notice the words "each of you." He speaks to every one of them.

True. The LORD says, "Even if Babylon ascends to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers I send will come against her…" (Jeremiah 51:53). Babylon can climb as high as she wants and fortify her stronghold. The destroyers He sends still come against her.

Right. The verse says, "For the LORD will destroy Babylon; He will silence her mighty voice." (Jeremiah 51:55). Notice the word "mighty." This isn't a small voice getting hushed, friend. It's her strongest one going quiet.

Yes. The LORD of Hosts says, "Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled, and her high gates consumed by fire." (Jeremiah 51:58). Thick walls and high gates are the parts a city leans on, and both get named here. I think that's a lot of building to see go.

I'd love to say yes, since all that work should count for something. But the LORD of Hosts says otherwise. "So the labor of the people will be for nothing…" (Jeremiah 51:58). Nothing means nothing, friend.
